DI-147F7B47.description: The previous implementation maintained a global dict keyed by cancer site. Every episode sharing that site key received the same specialist_seen flag and specialist_visit_date, irrespective of temporal ordering. This caused historic specialist visits to contaminate later same-site referrals, producing false stale_post_specialist episode closures and incorrect NCDA audit specialist-seen rates.
DI-147F7B47.rationale: The previous implementation maintained a global dict keyed by cancer site. Every episode sharing that site key received the same specialist_seen flag and specialist_visit_date, irrespective of temporal ordering. This caused historic specialist visits to contaminate later same-site referrals, producing false stale_post_specialist episode closures and incorrect NCDA audit specialist-seen rates.
DI-147F7B47.requirement: The episode detection system SHALL attribute each specialist visit anchor to at most one EpisodeOfCare node using a per-episode temporal claiming algorithm. A specialist visit is eligible for an episode only if (a) its encounter date is on or after the episode referral date, (b) its encounter date is on or before the episode window end date (diagnosis date for closed episodes; referral_date + 365 days for open episodes), and (c) its cancer site key is compatible with the episode site key. Episodes are processed in referral-date order (earliest first) so that earlier pathways have priority over later pathways when multiple episodes share a site key. Each visit that is successfully claimed is removed from the pool and cannot be attributed to any other episode.
DI-147F7B47.title: Per-episode temporal claiming of specialist visit anchors

DI-17AA6900.description: The consensus architecture expects the arbitrator to resolve a two-way split -- it normally returns one of the two existing verdicts. A third verdict (distinct from both primary verdicts) is a statistically unusual outcome. While it can arise from genuine model uncertainty, it is also the expected output pattern for a successful prompt injection or jailbreak that produces a non-standard verdict string. Making this case explicitly observable in logs enables post-incident forensic analysis and ongoing anomaly monitoring.
DI-17AA6900.rationale: The consensus architecture expects the arbitrator to resolve a two-way split -- it normally returns one of the two existing verdicts. A third verdict (distinct from both primary verdicts) is a statistically unusual outcome. While it can arise from genuine model uncertainty, it is also the expected output pattern for a successful prompt injection or jailbreak that produces a non-standard verdict string. Making this case explicitly observable in logs enables post-incident forensic analysis and ongoing anomaly monitoring.
DI-17AA6900.requirement: The dual-model consensus runner (libs/llm_client/consensus.py) SHALL emit a WARNING-level log message with the keyword 'consensus.arbitrator_third_verdict' whenever the Sonnet arbitrator returns a verdict that differs from both the AWS and Azure primary model verdicts. The warning MUST include the arbitrator verdict, the AWS verdict, and the Azure verdict. This warning is an audit control signal: an unexpected third verdict from the arbitrator may indicate that an LLM model has been jailbroken, subjected to prompt injection, or is producing anomalous output.
DI-17AA6900.title: Consensus arbitrator third-verdict warning for anomaly detection

DI-3197332F.rationale: Disorder entities extracted from clinical text frequently appear in informational or historical context (e.g. eGFR for CKD monitoring where CKD is a test context, not an active diagnosis). DI-3197332F.requirement: The system SHALL classify disorder entities as active_diagnosis, informational, historical, or uncertain using dual-model consensus, with mode-aware fail-safe behaviour: HITL mode defaults to active_diagnosis (human will review), autonomous mode defaults to uncertain (do not code without confirmation)

DI-3FDBB57B.requirement: The system SHALL use a single unified LangGraph-based coding and audit agent as the exclusive runtime execution path for all clinical coding and pipeline jobs, with the training and runtime pipelines sharing the same post-processing functions, so that there is no divergence between paths and all coding outputs are traceable to a single versioned agent definition.
DI-3FDBB57B.title: Unified LangGraph coding agent as the single execution path for all coding and pipeline jobs

Guard SHALL NOT fire on disorder concepts regardless of PT content.

Guard SHALL NOT alter entities whose assertion is already "present".

DI-527848A8.requirement: The staging enrichment subgraph SHALL derive stage only from encounter text inside a fixed post-diagnosis window of STAGING_WINDOW_DAYS days (default 90) starting at the episode's diagnosis_date. If no evidence rows match the specialty marker, the filter SHALL fall back to the unfiltered rows to avoid producing a null stage where the window contained relevant evidence that simply did not mention the site keyword.

DI-55C1C21F.description: Today the dry-run review queue runs toLower(c.text) CONTAINS toLower($search) server-side and decorates the returned rows client-side via DI-LEO-AI-523 with the same chip + highlight vocabulary as /care/encounters. That works for cosmetic parity but does not let the reviewer find synonym matches on the page: if a candidate sentence wrote 'mass' but the reviewer typed 'lump', the row is filtered OUT before the chip layer sees it. Pushing the same deterministic expansion into the cypher closes the loop so the dry-run queue actually returns the same rows as /care/encounters would. Keeping the typo / synonym maps in a single shared module (libs/search/term_expansion.py) is what keeps the three surfaces -- host search, drawer, dry-run -- on the same vocabulary as the product evolves.
DI-55C1C21F.rationale: Today the dry-run review queue runs toLower(c.text) CONTAINS toLower($search) server-side and decorates the returned rows client-side via DI-LEO-AI-523 with the same chip + highlight vocabulary as /care/encounters. That works for cosmetic parity but does not let the reviewer find synonym matches on the page: if a candidate sentence wrote 'mass' but the reviewer typed 'lump', the row is filtered OUT before the chip layer sees it. Pushing the same deterministic expansion into the cypher closes the loop so the dry-run queue actually returns the same rows as /care/encounters would. Keeping the typo / synonym maps in a single shared module (libs/search/term_expansion.py) is what keeps the three surfaces -- host search, drawer, dry-run -- on the same vocabulary as the product evolves.
DI-55C1C21F.requirement: The /admin/training Candidates and Gold-label review-queue endpoints (GET /api/training/candidates and GET /api/training/gold-labels) SHALL expand the reviewer's free-text search query using the same deterministic typo and synonym vocabulary as the host encounter search on /care/encounters before the cypher filter is applied, so a query for 'lump' surfaces TrainingCandidate / GoldLabel rows that wrote 'mass', 'swelling', or 'nodule' in the same single page. A new pure-Python helper libs/search/term_expansion.py SHALL hold the single source of truth for the typo correction map (TYPO_MAP), synonym map (SYNONYM_MAP), and an expand_search_terms(query) function. The analytics-layer encounter_query_understanding.py SHALL be refactored to import the same maps and helper from this module. GET_TRAINING_CANDIDATES_PAGE / COUNT_TRAINING_CANDIDATES_PAGE / GET_GOLD_LABELS_PAGE / COUNT_GOLD_LABELS_PAGE SHALL accept an optional $terms parameter (lower-case array). When non-empty, the cypher OR-matches via ANY(t IN $terms WHERE toLower(c.text) CONTAINS t); when empty/NULL, falls back to the legacy $search substring filter via CASE for backward compatibility. The training router and neo4j_mcp tools SHALL forward the expanded terms to both page and count queries on the same request. Mirrors DI-LEO-AI-520 and DI-LEO-AI-523 (UN-LEO-AI-096).
DI-55C1C21F.title: DI-LEO-AI-526: Server-side search term expansion for the dry-run review queue

DI-6E6E985B.description: String test results (positive, negative, borderline) are the dominant result form in microbiology and immunology consultations. Pre-entity value ordering is common in GP system templates. Without these two extensions, observable entities leave the pipeline with obs.value = None despite a result being clearly present, degrading downstream abnormal detection and audit analytics.
DI-6E6E985B.rationale: String test results (positive, negative, borderline) are the dominant result form in microbiology and immunology consultations. Pre-entity value ordering is common in GP system templates. Without these two extensions, observable entities leave the pipeline with obs.value = None despite a result being clearly present, degrading downstream abnormal detection and audit analytics.
DI-6E6E985B.requirement: The post-processing Layer 6 value-unit linker SHALL be extended to: (1) attach string-based result descriptors (positive, negative, borderline, reactive, non-reactive, and all other terms in _RESULT_DESCRIPTOR_TEXTS) as obs[value] on the nearest observable_entity within 40 characters; (2) perform a raw-text window scan of up to 60 characters preceding an observable entity's start offset to capture numeric or string values that were not extracted as separate entity spans by the NER model; and (3) accept an optional encounter_text parameter so that both the entity-list path and the raw-text fallback path operate in a single function call without breaking existing callers.
DI-6E6E985B.title: Layer 6 value-unit linker extension for string descriptors and raw-text fallback

DI-7A7BFA0C.description: Prior behaviour skipped the vector branch whenever any lexical hit existed, even a weak fuzzy match. Weak lexical matches on ambiguous surface forms could suppress stronger semantic matches and drive incorrect SNOMED concept selection. Thresholding the skip keeps the hybrid retrieval effective where it matters (ambiguous/unusual terms) while preserving the latency saving for high-confidence lexical matches.
DI-7A7BFA0C.rationale: Prior behaviour skipped the vector branch whenever any lexical hit existed, even a weak fuzzy match. Weak lexical matches on ambiguous surface forms could suppress stronger semantic matches and drive incorrect SNOMED concept selection. Thresholding the skip keeps the hybrid retrieval effective where it matters (ambiguous/unusual terms) while preserving the latency saving for high-confidence lexical matches.
DI-7A7BFA0C.requirement: The CodingResolver SHALL run the vector-search branch whenever the top lexical score (exact + fulltext merged) is below a configurable threshold, defaulting to 0.70 (TERMINOLOGY_VECTOR_SKIP_SCORE). The vector branch SHALL be skipped only when the top lexical score meets or exceeds the threshold, OR when TERMINOLOGY_ENABLE_VECTOR=false. This rule SHALL apply to both the batched resolve() path and the single-term _resolve_single() path.
DI-7A7BFA0C.title: Terminology hybrid retrieval skips vector search only when top lexical score >= 0.7

DI-80DD8A47.requirement: The consensus runner used by the disorder gate and coding-verifier steps SHALL support two modes: (1) single-model (default) - one AWS Bedrock call at the configured tier with a strict-reminder parse-retry on parse failure; (2) dual-model (opt-in via CONSENSUS_DUAL_MODEL=true) - AWS small-tier and Azure small-tier judges run in parallel, an AWS big-tier arbitrator resolves disagreement or single-provider failure. The headline metric card that previously showed the '17' pathway-only cohort SHALL either use the canonical confirmed_cancer cohort (displaying 91 in the 2025 baseline dataset) or be relabelled '2WW-route diagnoses' with a tooltip explaining the narrower definition.

SimilarCandidatesBatch SHALL accept a search?: string prop forwarded by GoldDatasetPanel.tsx (the panel's debouncedSearch), expand it once per render via useMemo(() => expandSearchTerms(search)), per-row compute matchRationale = computeMatchRationale(item.text, expandedTerms) and highlightTerms = collectHighlightTerms(search, hitTerms), conditionally wrap the truncated row text in <HighlightedText testId='similar-candidate-row-highlight'>, and render a Box (data-testid 'similar-candidate-row-match-rationale') of up to 4 outlined Chips (data-testid 'similar-candidate-row-match-rationale-chip', variant='outlined', height 20, fontSize 0.65rem). DI-C0AD09D2.description: Post-fix investigation identified 14 genuinely unreferred confirmed-cancer episodes in 2025; 7 of those 14 (50%) are tagged cancer_type=breast, suggesting the current breast regex misses a meaningful fraction of breast 2WW referral letters. The existing regex matches breast, nipple, mammogra, mastectom, lumpectom, oncoplas, DCIS, LCIS, invasive ductal/lobular, HER2, ER/PR status, Ca breast - but not the common triple-assessment / breast-clinic / family-history phrasing that dominates general practice referral notes. Broadening the regex is the cheapest fix for this subset.
DI-C0AD09D2.rationale: Post-fix investigation identified 14 genuinely unreferred confirmed-cancer episodes in 2025; 7 of those 14 (50%) are tagged cancer_type=breast, suggesting the current breast regex misses a meaningful fraction of breast 2WW referral letters. The existing regex matches breast, nipple, mammogra, mastectom, lumpectom, oncoplas, DCIS, LCIS, invasive ductal/lobular, HER2, ER/PR status, Ca breast - but not the common triple-assessment / breast-clinic / family-history phrasing that dominates general practice referral notes. Broadening the regex is the cheapest fix for this subset.
DI-C0AD09D2.requirement: SPECIALTY_MARKERS[breast] in libs/clinical_scoping/specialty_markers.py SHALL match every UK-primary-care clinical surface form that reliably indicates the breast pathway, including: triple assessment, breast clinic, nipple discharge, family history of breast cancer, fibroadenoma references, ductal carcinoma, lobular carcinoma, areola, and sentinel lymph node biopsy. The extended regex SHALL achieve >= 90% recall on a corpus of 20 real 2025 breast encounter texts sampled from the dev graph and SHALL NOT falsely match generic chest/thorax/non-breast contexts.
DI-C0AD09D2.title: Breast specialty marker recall extension for UK primary-care vocabulary

DI-D2D0117E.description: An incorrect surface form mapping that was approved and has been in use affects every encounter processed since it was activated. Simply removing the mapping does not fix the historical records -- they remain coded with the wrong concept. The cascade creates a review task for each affected encounter, giving reviewers visibility and a workflow to correct or confirm each one. Without this, incorrect mappings leave a permanent trail of wrong codes in patient records.
DI-D2D0117E.rationale: An incorrect surface form mapping that was approved and has been in use affects every encounter processed since it was activated. Simply removing the mapping does not fix the historical records -- they remain coded with the wrong concept. The cascade creates a review task for each affected encounter, giving reviewers visibility and a workflow to correct or confirm each one. Without this, incorrect mappings leave a permanent trail of wrong codes in patient records.
DI-D2D0117E.requirement: The system SHALL provide a surface form revocation endpoint that removes a MAPS_TO relationship, marks the SurfaceFormTask as revoked, and creates CodingReview nodes for every encounter coded after the surface form's first_used_at date where a DOCUMENTS relationship uses the revoked concept with source=provisional, so that affected records can be corrected or confirmed by a reviewer.
DI-D2D0117E.title: Surface form revocation with cascade CodingReview creation

DI-EC96F102.description: A critical bug was identified where the LLM extraction step inferred Chronic kidney disease stage 1 (disorder) from an eGFR measurement of 69 mL/min. The eGFR text included CKD-EPI (a formula name) which the LLM misinterpreted as a diagnostic abbreviation. Inferring diagnoses from lab values is clinically unsafe because a lab value alone does not constitute a diagnosis, the inferred diagnosis may be incorrect, and a false diagnosis in the patient record can influence care decisions, audit outcomes, and quality measures.
DI-EC96F102.rationale: A critical bug was identified where the LLM extraction step inferred Chronic kidney disease stage 1 (disorder) from an eGFR measurement of 69 mL/min. The eGFR text included CKD-EPI (a formula name) which the LLM misinterpreted as a diagnostic abbreviation. Inferring diagnoses from lab values is clinically unsafe because a lab value alone does not constitute a diagnosis, the inferred diagnosis may be incorrect, and a false diagnosis in the patient record can influence care decisions, audit outcomes, and quality measures.
DI-EC96F102.requirement: The coding pipeline SHALL NOT infer a clinical diagnosis from a lab result value. Lab measurements (e.g. eGFR, HbA1c, creatinine, sodium, haemoglobin, cholesterol, TSH, troponin, PSA, LDH, amylase, lipase, procalcitonin, NT-proBNP, CK/CPK, lactate, AFP, CA-125, CEA) SHALL be coded only as observable entities with their numeric value and unit. A disorder entity SHALL only be generated when the encounter text explicitly states a diagnosis. The lab-value guard SHALL operate on a per-entity sentence window (not the full encounter text) to avoid false suppression of legitimate diagnoses in other parts of the encounter.
DI-EC96F102.title: Lab-value guard prevents diagnostic inference from observable measurements

DI-FC264BBF.description: Live investigation found 75 of 91 confirmed cancer episodes in 2025 had ep.referral_date set but no IS_PART_OF{milestone_type:referral} edge, because the builder rejected every referral whose site tag was unknown then silently wrote the diagnosis encounter date back into ep.referral_date as a fallback. The effect was a data-integrity lie: referral_date on 75 of 91 episodes was really the diagnosis date, and the 2WW-route metric undercounted by 3-4x. The two-pass fallback matches NHS reality, where a non-trivial fraction of 2WW referral letters lack an unambiguous body-site tag.
DI-FC264BBF.rationale: Live investigation found 75 of 91 confirmed cancer episodes in 2025 had ep.referral_date set but no IS_PART_OF{milestone_type:referral} edge, because the builder rejected every referral whose site tag was unknown then silently wrote the diagnosis encounter date back into ep.referral_date as a fallback. The effect was a data-integrity lie: referral_date on 75 of 91 episodes was really the diagnosis date, and the 2WW-route metric undercounted by 3-4x. The two-pass fallback matches NHS reality, where a non-trivial fraction of 2WW referral letters lack an unambiguous body-site tag.
DI-FC264BBF.requirement: The episode builder SHALL match each cancer diagnosis anchor to a preceding referral anchor using a two-pass strategy. Pass 1 keeps current strict same-site behaviour: only a referral whose site key equals the diagnosis site or is non_site_specific may be claimed. Any diagnosis still unmatched after Pass 1 runs through Pass 2, which claims the nearest unclaimed referral within DIAG_LOOKBACK_DAYS regardless of site key, subject to MIN_REFERRAL_TO_DIAG_DAYS. Episodes produced via Pass 2 SHALL be tagged ep.referral_match_method = fallback_any_site so downstream audit surfaces can distinguish strict from fallback claims. When NO referral can be claimed, ep.referral_date SHALL NOT be synthesised from the diagnosis encounter date; it SHALL be persisted as NULL, and ep.referral_inferred SHALL be false.
DI-FC264BBF.title: Two-pass referral matching with strict-then-fallback claim and honest NULL
